2	status: proposed
3	date: 2026-10-23
4	parts: visuals, views, agent, architecture, turns, server
5	
6	## Context
7	Sessions should show flows and maps of the parts a change touches, drawn with Prelude's own design system. The agent's words go through Koda's `renderMarkdown`, which escapes raw HTML, so the agent can't write markup into the chat and shouldn't. `renderMarkdown` turns every fence into `<pre><code class="language-x">` with its body escaped, and offers no hook. Its fence tag must be `[A-Za-z0-9_-]*` with nothing after it: anything else isn't a fence, and its closing line then opens a code block that swallows the rest of the message. Koda's custom-element renderers are for host-owned media types, too heavy for a transcript entry.
8	
9	## Decision
10	A visual is a fenced block tagged `prelude-<kind>-<version>`. Version 1 has `prelude-flow-1` (an optional `# title`, then `1. <part id>: <text>` steps, as in `flows/*.md`) and `prelude-map-1` (one `<part id>` per line, optionally followed by `: <note>`, drawn on the whole map with those parts highlighted). A new part, `visuals`, holds a registry of kinds: for each, a parser per version, the check, and its lines for the prompt. Adding a visual takes a registry entry and a `_visual-<kind>.eta` partial. `views` splits a message on top-level fences using Koda's own fence rule, before rendering, and renders the text between with `renderMarkdown`. A block `visuals` parses and checks becomes its partial. Anything else stays a code block, and the agent isn't told. A part id is checked against the architecture of the session's branch as it stands when the entry is shown. The transcript keeps the agent's text as written. 1	# Prelude architecture
2	
3	Prelude is a tool for designing and then building an app with an agent: you pick a project, chat with the Claude Code CLI, and watch the design appear beside the chat. It runs as one Node server (plain `node:http`, views in Eta, Koda in the page) on localhost:4200, optionally inside a Tauri desktop window. Everything it produces is files in the project's `prelude/` folder, each design worked on in its own git branch and worktree. Agent-written views render in a sandboxed child process, and each design is served on its own preview origin.
4	
5	## Layers
6	
7	1. Windows
8	2. Entry points
9	3. Pages
10	4. Agent and live state
11	5. Designs and hosting
12	6. Project files
13	7. Shared helpers
14	8. Outside
15	
16	## Principles
17

I've designed visuals in the transcript: six new states (09–14), new partials, and 11 proposed rules. I haven't seen any of it rendered, so Prelude's check after this turn is the first real test, at about 1000px as well as wide.

**How it works:** to change the transcript, the Design page's route had to come back into the design, with every view it includes. Only `_entry` and `_live-entry` changed; the rest are straight copies. An agent's message is now a list of pieces in the order it was written: words, a flow, a map, a placeholder while one is being written, or a block that couldn't be read. A new partial draws each kind.

**What each state shows:**
- **09 A flow and a map:** a 4-part flow (a list in the 26rem chat), then the agent's map with "Would change" on three parts. On a marked map, the other parts show only their names, so a map of the whole project fits the column.
- **10 Several visuals:** words, a 5-part flow, words, a 3-part flow, words, a map, words.
- **11 Visual not drawn:** three blocks, each shown as written with its fence and tag, and a muted "Not drawn: …" line under it. The reasons are parts that aren't in the architecture, a line in the wrong format, and an unknown kind (`prelude-chart-1`).
- **12 Popped out:** the same conversation as 09 with the chat full width. The flow gets columns and the map's layer labels sit beside their parts.
- **13 Drawing a visual:** while the agent streams, a finished flow is drawn at once. The map it's still writing is a placeholder saying "Drawing a map of the parts…".
- **14 Ask and fix:** a fix's conversation, where the chat is about 46rem wide. A 4-part flow gets columns there; five or more parts stay a list. After the fix, Prelude adds its own entry: a map with "Changed" on the parts the edited files belong to.

Every part on a flow or map links to `/f/<project>/architecture/parts/<id>`.

**Rules:** R-6jw, R-p3e, R-k9u, R-x2a, R-f7c, R-0hq, R-m4v, R-b8s, R-w5g, R-c1y and R-9tz, all *proposed*. They cover what's checked (part ids against the session branch's architecture as it is now, the format, the kind and version) and what happens when a check fails. A failed block shows as written with the reason. Renaming a part later turns old blocks back into code. A project with no architecture draws nothing. The agent is never told a visual wasn't drawn.

**Two changes to the design system:**
- **Flow parts can be links.** The column heads hold mouse-only links, and each step's part name is a link that shows in its box when it has keyboard focus.
- **A transcript rule was padding the visuals.** `.entry ul` added padding to the map's and flow's lists inside a message, so it's now `.entry :where(ul)`. The same fix removes a stray indent from images in sent messages.

Both are in the design system's NOTES.md and its gallery.

No architecture decision was needed: this fits D-v3x and what the views part says it uses.

**What changes for you and the build:**
- Agent messages are now wrapped in an extra container, so pages in the existing states will differ from their approved screens. You'll need to approve them again.
